mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months raises the cost of capital, reducing present value of future corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% and remains elevated for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) over three months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which lowers real interest rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) combined with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving average signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate revenue and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly AND HOUST > 6-month moving average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals labor market strength, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of aggressive monetary easing (FEDFUNDS falling >0.5% per month).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall below 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS not falling >0.5% per month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes when FEDFUNDS is not aggressively easing, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance in those episodes.
